text.title: EF Core Data Layer Core Rules
text.summary: 10 testable rules grounding the EF Core data-layer methodology. Each rule pairs a binary check + sourced rationale.

rule.statement: Every entity MUST have a dedicated `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` class under `Data/Configurations/` covering table name, keys, indexes, max lengths, default-value SQL and cascade behaviour. `OnModelCreating` MUST call `ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly(...)` and contain no inline `builder.Entity<T>().Property(...)` calls. Data annotations (`[Required]`, `[MaxLength]`) on entities are forbidden.

rationale.source: Microsoft EF Core docs — Configuring entity types

rule.rationale: Inline configuration in `OnModelCreating` grows unbounded and hides entity-specific mapping detail behind one giant method; per-entity classes keep diffs scoped. The fluent API also covers the full feature surface (HasDefaultValueSql, owned types, shadow properties) that annotations only partly reach, and annotations split the mapping across an attribute and a class.

rule.statement: Every read-only query path MUST call `AsNoTracking()` — or `AsNoTrackingWithIdentityResolution()` when navigation identity matters — and project to a DTO or anonymous type before materialization.

rationale.source: Microsoft EF Core performance guide + Query tracking docs

rule.rationale: The change tracker bloats memory and CPU on read paths, and projecting short-circuits entity hydration that nobody will use.

rule.statement: Repository methods MUST NOT return `IQueryable<T>`. They MUST materialize (`ToListAsync`, `ToArrayAsync`, `FirstOrDefaultAsync`) before crossing the layer boundary, and return `PagedResult<TDto>` — `{Items, TotalCount, Page, PageSize}` — for list queries.
rule.rationale: Returning `IQueryable` leaks query execution outside the persistence boundary: callers can extend the query past the constraints the repository intended, and the DbContext has to outlive the repository or the query fails on a disposed context.

rule.statement: Any query whose `.Include()` chain covers ≥ 2 collection navigations MUST add `.AsSplitQuery()`. Single-collection or scalar-only Include chains MAY keep the default single-query mode.

rationale.source: Microsoft EF Core docs — Single vs split queries

rule.rationale: Joining over two collection navigations produces a Cartesian product (rows × rows): 100 orders × 10 items × 50 discounts is 50k rows for one page. `AsSplitQuery` issues separate SELECTs and merges client-side.

rule.statement: Entities are POCOs with `private set` properties, a private or protected parameterless constructor for EF materialization, and collections exposed as `IReadOnlyCollection<T>` over a private backing field initialised at construction.

rationale.source: DDD Reference + EF Core materialization docs

rule.rationale: Public setters let any caller bypass the invariants the constructor enforces; the parameterless constructor is what EF needs to materialize a row without going through them. An externally mutable collection is the same hole in another shape.

rule.statement: Migrations are append-only. Once a migration is merged to the deploy branch its `*.cs` file MUST NOT be edited or renamed. Fixes go into a new migration with a verb-prefixed name (`AlterUserAddIsActive`, `BackfillOrderNumber`, `FixTypoInOrdersTable`).

rationale.source: Microsoft EF Core docs — Migrations + team workflow

rule.rationale: A migration is a schema-history record, not code. Editing one after deploy makes environments diverge — prod applied the old version, staging the new — and rerun-safety depends on the sequence matching `__EFMigrationsHistory` on every database.

rule.statement: Every aggregate root MUST carry an optimistic-concurrency token: `[Timestamp] byte[] RowVersion` (SqlServer) or `[ConcurrencyCheck]` `xmin uint` (Postgres). Concurrent updates without a token are forbidden.
rule.rationale: Without a token, EF's last-write-wins silently corrupts data under concurrent edits.

rule.statement: Bulk updates and deletes MUST use `ExecuteUpdateAsync`/`ExecuteDeleteAsync` (EF Core 7+) — not load + mutate + SaveChanges loops.
rule.rationale: Load-mutate-save round-trips a row at a time; `ExecuteUpdateAsync` runs one SQL statement and never touches the change tracker.

rule.statement: Cross-cutting audit fields (`CreatedAt`, `UpdatedAt`, `UpdatedBy`) MUST be populated by a `SaveChangesInterceptor` registered once on the `DbContext`. Per-entity configuration MUST NOT set these in every class.
rule.rationale: Per-entity duplication drifts; one interceptor enforces a single canonical implementation across the model.

rule.statement: Migrations applied to shared dev or prod databases MUST be reviewed as SQL via `dotnet ef migrations script` BEFORE `dotnet ef database update`. Destructive operations (`DROP COLUMN`, `DROP TABLE`) require an explicit human checkpoint.
rule.rationale: Code-level diff hides destructive SQL (e.g. cascade FK reshuffle); SQL review surfaces the actual schema delta.
